clue.text: Bank on a vehicle having interior decoration

indicators.note: a car having something inside it holds it within its body, so the decoration sits in the middle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour, a decoration; 'interior' tells us it goes inside

explanation.surface: A banking manager's car with a fancy interior refit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior' belongs with the decoration, marking it as the piece put inside. A road's camber is its banked slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A road's sideways slope or tilt, built so traffic corners safely, is its bank.

clue.text: Journalists after work get abuse

indicators.note: placed after means the journalists come second, following the word for work

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work in music
the press is a collective name for journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters, once their shift ends, get insulted.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse people under one's power is to treat them cruelly and unjustly, a harsh form of tyranny.

clue.text: Painter set against firm

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
stable means firm and steady

explanation.surface: An artist is placed in opposition to a company.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was an English landscape painter. 'firm' looks like a company noun but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was a celebrated English landscape artist.

clue.text: Save contention over a certain point

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so the fight comes first

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or quarrel, a contention
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Rescue the argument just before a particular point is made.
explanation.walkthrough: To scrape is to save money with difficulty, as in scrimping and scraping.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape is to economise hard and put money by, little by little.

clue.text: Be a dog, work out in the wine bar

indicators.note: to work out a puzzle is to rearrange things until they fit, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to act like a dog and exercise in a Spanish tavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish cellar or shop selling wine, often a small bar.

clue.text: Wraps up the party on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the party comes first

parts.note: a band is a group or party of people
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: The group finishes off the celebration punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wraps up' reads as 'finishes' but means binds with dressings.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind a wound with strips of dressing is to wrap it up.

clue.text: Many object to the same thing

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword shorthand for many
it is a pronoun for an object or thing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plenty of people raise an objection to an identical item.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to say the same again, a repetition of what was said before.

clue.text: A pest both naive and knowing

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive
fly is slang for sharp or knowing

explanation.surface: A nuisance who is somehow both innocent and worldly-wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both' just joins the two halves; the clue's contrast of naive and knowing is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly are aphids that infest garden plants, a common insect nuisance.

clue.text: Move towards a very soft kind of fish

parts.note: PP (pianissimo) is the musical direction for very soft
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Go up to a quiet sort of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach is to come nearer, to draw close.

clue.text: A woolly-minded manual worker

parts.note: woolly-minded suggests vague thinking, but here it means someone whose mind is on wool, working by hand with needles

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes garments from yarn with needles works with their hands and thinks about wool.

clue.text: A Scottish writer gets overheated

definitions.meaning: something that is too hot is scorched

explanation.surface: A Scots author loses their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns was the Scottish poet, and something too hot is scorched or singed.

clue.text: Average sum outstanding

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
an amount is a sum

explanation.surface: An ordinary total that is still owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' suggests a debt still unpaid, but here means supreme.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme or of the highest importance, standing out above all others.

clue.text: Turmoil some sad old people cause

indicators.note: some of the words means only a part of them is taken, a run of letters inside

explanation.surface: Gloomy elderly folk stir up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado is fuss and bustle, a state of commotion.

clue.text: The country's in the red, it's said, yet again

indicators.note: the country is in the red means it sits inside the word for red

parts.note: taken as written, the colour
a state is a country; the apostrophe s reads as is

explanation.surface: The nation is in debt, people claim once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' looks like debt, but the word RED is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate something is to express it again.

clue.text: Invest pounds in comforts-they're so supportive

indicators.note: to invest money in something is to put it inside, so the pounds go into the comforts

parts.note: eases means comforts or relieves
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Putting money into comforts is reassuring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they're so supportive' sounds like kind friends, but an easel supports an artist's canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's stand holds up a painting, so these stands are literally supportive.

clue.text: Flat broke-meant to retain a bit

indicators.note: to retain something is to keep it within, so the bit sits inside the rearranged letters
broke means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a part is a bit

explanation.surface: A penniless person meant to hang on to a share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' looks like the definition's partner (a flat broke person) but is the anagram signal; 'retain' keeps the bit inside the rearranged letters, right after their first A.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a set of rooms on one floor, a residence in a block.

clue.text: Show off about one's heavenly place

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the display wraps around the other piece

parts.note: to parade is to show off
one is I, and the apostrophe s reads as is

explanation.surface: Flaunting yourself around your own divine home.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is heaven, the abode of the blessed.

clue.text: Left before midday to organise strike

parts.note: AM is ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Leave in the morning to arrange a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to organise strike' suggests industrial action, but strike means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is to beat or thrash someone, a hard blow.

clue.text: Head off cracked fan!

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: rent means torn or split open, cracked

explanation.surface: Decapitate the crazy supporter!
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter of a cause or person.

clue.text: A little waspish venomous creature

indicators.note: a little of the word means only a small run of its letters is taken

explanation.surface: A slightly irritable poisonous animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The asp is a venomous snake of Egypt.

clue.text: No gentleman set about a lady, as is realised

indicators.note: set about means placed round, so the cad surrounds the lady

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, no gentleman
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A bounder attacked a woman, as is now known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' sounds like attacking, but means placed around. Realised means converted into money.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets realised are turned into money, as a cheque is when exchanged for notes.

clue.text: Pass for an officer

explanation.definitionFit: A col is a gap between peaks, and Col is short for colonel, a senior officer.

clue.text: Dons exhibiting particular ability?

definitions.meaning: dons are university lecturers, collectively the teaching staff
a gift or talent for something

explanation.definitionFit: The teaching staff of a university are its faculty, and a faculty is also an aptitude or talent.

clue.text: Subdued, so possibly move with care

indicators.note: possibly means these letters might be arranged another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling meek, you might shift things gently.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcame means conquered or defeated, as an enemy is put down.

clue.text: Chase-even changing trains

indicators.note: changing means the letters swap places, so they are rearranged

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, where trains run

explanation.surface: A pursuit, even with a change of trains.
explanation.walkthrough: Venery is an old word for hunting; 'Chase' is the noun, the hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Venery is the old art of hunting game, the pursuit with hounds.

clue.text: Expected to divide the tip provided

indicators.note: to divide something is to split it, so the expected piece splits the tip in two

parts.note: an end is a tip
due means expected

explanation.surface: Anticipated to share the gratuity provided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a gratuity, but means an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Endued means endowed or supplied with a quality.

clue.text: A game hardly worth a mention?

definitions.meaning: a table game rolling balls into holes

explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a pinball-like table game, and the word also means a mere trifle.

clue.text: A sailing man made a meal and let up

parts.note: an AB is an able seaman, a sailor
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: A sailor dined and relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or die down.

clue.text: Form of fungoid growth

definitions.meaning: a shape used to form things
a furry fungus growing on damp food

explanation.definitionFit: A mould shapes material poured into it, and mould is also a fungus.

clue.text: Keep using dialect

indicators.note: using the letters means working them into a new arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continue speaking in the local tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' reads as a verb but is a castle's stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the stronghold of a castle, a fortress.

clue.text: The beast accepting catch is far from fair

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the beast holds the catch inside

parts.note: a brute is a beast
a net is a catch of fish

explanation.surface: The animal taking a haul is very unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far from fair' suggests injustice, but means dark-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with dark hair is the opposite of a blonde.

clue.text: Concerned with foreign money, being up-to date

parts.note: re means regarding, concerned with
a cent is a coin of many foreign currencies

explanation.surface: Dealing with overseas currency is modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Recent means modern or of late.
